gloss: to interact, to come into contact

forms.label: Past polite
forms.negative: {触|ふ}れ{合|あ}いませんでした

forms.label: ている past
forms.negative: {触|ふ}れ{合|あ}っていなかった

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {触|ふ}れ{合|あ}っていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to touch each other, to come into physical contact
definitions.explanation: For two things or people to physically touch or brush against each other.

definitions.gloss: to interact, to have contact with, to connect
definitions.explanation: To have personal interaction or meaningful contact with people, nature, or culture.

examples.japanese: {手|て}と{手|て}が{触|ふ}れ{合|あ}った。
{肩|かた}が{触|ふ}れ{合|あ}うほど{近|ちか}くに{座|すわ}った。
examples.english: We sat so close that our shoulders touched.

examples.japanese: {満員電車|まんいんでんしゃ}では{見知|みし}らぬ{人|ひと}と{体|からだ}が{触|ふ}れ{合|あ}う。
examples.english: On a packed train, your body comes into contact with strangers.

examples.japanese: {自然|しぜん}と{触|ふ}れ{合|あ}う。
{地元|じもと}の{人|ひと}たちと{触|ふ}れ{合|あ}う{機会|きかい}があった。
examples.english: I had an opportunity to interact with the local people.

examples.japanese: {動物|どうぶつ}と{触|ふ}れ{合|あ}える{体験型|たいけんがた}の{牧場|ぼくじょう}は{子|こ}どもに{人気|にんき}がある。
examples.english: Hands-on farms where you can interact with animals are popular with children.

notes:
CONJUGATION (godan, {合|あ}う stem):
- Negative: {触|ふ}れ{合|あ}わない
- Te-form: {触|ふ}れ{合|あ}って
- Past: {触|ふ}れ{合|あ}った

TRANSITIVITY:
Intransitive. The {合|あ}う suffix indicates mutual or reciprocal action.

USAGE:
Sense 2 is very common in tourism, education, and community contexts. The noun form {触|ふ}れ{合|あ}い (interaction, contact) is widely used: {触|ふ}れ{合|あ}いの{場|ば} (a place for interaction).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {自然|しぜん}と{触|ふ}れ{合|あ}う: to connect with nature
- {動物|どうぶつ}と{触|ふ}れ{合|あ}う: to interact with animals
- {人|ひと}と{触|ふ}れ{合|あ}う: to have contact with people
- {文化|ぶんか}に{触|ふ}れ{合|あ}う: to come into contact with a culture
